accuracy.evidence: Every claim matches the named guidance: Development Matters 2021 PSED (children are calmed by their key person before they calm themselves; 3 and 4 year olds grow in confidence in new social situations), the EYFS statutory framework 2024 key person requirement, Bowlby 1969 and Ainsworth et al. 1978 (a trusted adult as a secure base), and AAP HealthyChildren.org and ZERO TO THREE separation advice (always say goodbye, keep it short and the same each day, do not sneak out, tie the return to a part of the day). The lesson never promises a clock time and never says feelings are wrong; it separates feelings (OK) from hurting actions (not OK). Numeric items are counts within 10.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the real worries and slips around separation: the grown-up might not come back (week step, challenge tag gone), expecting them right after the hug or 'when I cry' (picture-plan prediction, tag clock), believing a sneaky exit is kinder (goodbye prediction, Grown-up sneaks out card, tag sneak), long clinging goodbyes (Hold on card, tag long), crying means naughty (Mia prediction, tag naughty), and waiting alone at the door instead of going to the key person (Wait by the door card, tag alone).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagbyebye is built on this topic's own mechanism: a nursery picture timetable walked in order with the grown-up at the end, a 3-slot goodbye routine that rejects sneaking out and clinging, an OK / Not OK sort of goodbye feelings and actions, a worry cloud that shrinks with each real comfort strategy and stays big for waiting at the door, and a 5-day week showing the return every day. Gate: under 30% shingle overlap with every other flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child finds when the grown-up returns by walking the plan (tapping the grown-up card early says 'Not yet! Your grown-up comes after story time'), feels why a goodbye beats sneaking out through the card feedback, sees the worry cloud shrink only for cuddle, teddy, breaths and a game, and builds trust by watching the return 5 days in a row. Each done line confirms what the child just did in one sentence.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab then disproves: 'Right after the hug' (the plan puts the grown-up after story time), 'Yes, then no tears' for sneaking out (the goodbye step rejects the sneak card and explains why), and 'Yes' to Mia being naughty for crying (the sort puts Crying in OK). Each step's done message reveals the locked-in prediction.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions; every wrong option is tagged to its own slip with its own message: gone ('Your grown-up always comes back'), clock ('The picture plan shows when'), sneak, long, naughty ('Sad, worried or cross feelings are OK. Hurting is not') and alone ('Go to your key person, then choose a game'). In-step feedback names the slip too, e.g. 'Holding on makes the goodbye long and hard'.

readability.evidence: Family lesson for ages 3 to 4: kid text in very short sentences of everyday words ('A hug. A wave at the window.'), within the learn/readability.py limit; adult text within its limit. Every card on the canvas is a picture with 1 to 6 words at 12 to 16 px or more, so a child who cannot read can do each step while a grown-up reads the heading.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passes (no filler phrases, under 12% six-word overlap with any other lesson). Each kid paragraph teaches one point (when the grown-up returns, what a good goodbye is, feelings OK but hurting not, what makes the worry smaller); adult paragraphs give the curriculum link, why to use events not clock times, named mistakes with sources, and a lab summary.

mobile.evidence: Checked on iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark: the picture plan is 2 rows of 3 cards about 110 by 120 px, goodbye slots fill the width, the OK / Not OK boxes are half the width each, the worry helpers wrap to 3 columns, and the week is 2 rows of large day cards. The young class gives 56 px buttons under the canvas; nothing is clipped.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button: 'Go to Snack' for each later picture, 'Put in my goodbye: Hug', OK and Not OK labelled with the card ('Crying is OK'), 'Try: Hold my teddy from home', and 'Next day: Tuesday'. say() updates the canvas aria-label and the polite live region after each action; the walk gate's axe run is clean (WCAG 2.1 AA) in both themes on desktop and iPhone.
